magicRules: The first circle continually produces water. Gutters and buckets manage it without stopping it.
Six magical complications remain: endless water, flowers, one talking duck, twelve ducks, giant flower and bubbles. Twelve ducks is a cast count, not a quota of magical mishaps.
First duck speech remains scene-58. Before that the ordinary plastic toy is not presented as a hero or a prediction.
Scenes50/51 are removed. There was no earlier hiccup or partial reverse experiment; scene-70 is only a question about the source.
At87 and114 PinPin observes the full-size bath and the circular source. He wonders whether reversing his original drawing direction changes the flow.
Scenes116–118 show a tentative reverse stroke, thinner flow and return when he stops;119–121 complete the reverse circuit. Mama asks, child proposes and tests.
The bath stays full-size throughout. There is no shrinking or restoration spell.
Existing water is cleaned physically and the aqueduct is removed. The whole family carries the twelve ducks to a real lake and releases them.
Bubbles81–86 are provisionally retained pending the user's clarification; no raincloud or later revoked mishaps follow them.
reviewRules: Previous productions remain immutable; only explicitly inspected reuse entries copy exact selected bytes and lineage.
Awake people remain alert, curious, concentrated, wry or briefly annoyed; no drained faces or slumped exhaustion. Natural shared-bed sleep is allowed.
All four hedgehog family members remain distinct and share the same broad bed. The infant is never submerged.
The ordinary yellow flexible-plastic duck has white eyes, black pupils and an orange bill. First speech occurs at58, without earlier hero framing or anticipation.
From66 the family contains exactly two adult-size ducks and ten smaller ducks; close crops may show a subset, never an additional thirteenth duck.
Papa actually jumps; Mama joins with PomPom held above water and PinPin joins with Papa's help.
Permanent room topology stays fixed; the bath has solid continuous wooden walls and floor at every scale. The rust rug remains underneath it.
Temporary gutters use a broad collector and descending supports through existing doors; pails and cloths catch residual drips.
Each mishap addresses an established consequence. Parent participation supports the child without supplying the final solution.
